statement: Ella puts 7 beads on a string. It looks the same read from either end. From the left, the first 4 beads are blue, green, blue, blue. How many beads are blue?

choices.misconception: I counted only the blue beads among the last 3 beads, the ones I had to work out.
I counted only the blue beads I was told about and did not work out the other 3 beads.
I copied the first 3 beads onto the other end but forgot to count the middle bead.
I copied all 4 beads onto the other end, so I counted the middle bead twice.

hints: Bead 1 must match bead 7. Which bead must match bead 2?

Reading the same from both ends means the string is a mirror picture of itself around its middle bead. Pair each bead with the bead the same distance from the other end. The middle bead has no partner.
Bead 4 is the middle bead. Bead 5 matches bead 3, bead 6 matches bead 2, and bead 7 matches bead 1.

solutions.reliable: With 7 beads, bead 4 is in the middle. Bead 5 copies bead 3 (blue), bead 6 copies bead 2 (green) and bead 7 copies bead 1 (blue). The string is blue, green, blue, blue, blue, green, blue, which has 5 blue beads. The idea to keep: in a mirror pattern every piece has a partner except the one sitting on the mirror line.
solutions.elegant: The 3 beads left of the middle include 2 blue beads, so the 3 beads on the right include 2 more. The middle bead is blue too: 2 + 2 + 1 = 5. The idea to keep: count one side, double it, then add whatever sits on the mirror line.

whyOnTest: Line symmetry: the middle bead sits on the mirror line, so it is counted once, and counting it twice is the usual slip.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
